whoIntro: You’ve probably done therapy before. You can name your patterns, maybe even trace them back to where they started. And yet the same feelings keep hijacking the present, the same relationship dynamics keep repeating, and the gap between understanding and changing hasn’t closed.
whoListLabel: People usually reach out to me when:
whoList: The creative work that once felt alive now feels like a grind, or you’ve lost touch with why you started.
Life in a creative industry (the unpredictable work, the visibility, the rejection) has worn down your sense of who you are outside of it.
Old trauma keeps showing up in the present: in your body, your reactions, your relationships.
You keep landing in the same painful dynamic, just with different people.
You look like you have it together, and underneath you feel restless, disconnected, or tired of keeping your guard up.
As a couple, intimacy and sex have stalled, and talking about it turns into a fight or a silence.
As a couple, you’re caught in loops of defensiveness and distance where neither of you feels met.
fitYesLabel: This is likely a good fit if:
fitYesList: You want depth, not a quick fix or a stack of coping worksheets.
You’re ready for weekly sessions. This work unfolds over months, not weeks.
You want a therapist who is engaged and direct, and who will challenge you when it counts.
You’re curious about what’s happening in your body and in the room, not only in your story.
fitNoLabel: It may not be the right fit if:
fitNoList: You’re looking for coaching or short-term, skills-only work.
You want a therapist who mostly listens and nods.
approachParagraph1: Insight matters, but it’s rarely enough on its own. In our sessions we slow down and pay attention to what’s happening right now: in your body, your emotions, and the space between us. That’s where old patterns show up live, and where they can actually change.
approachParagraph2: I’m engaged, direct, and collaborative. I won’t just nod and take notes. I’m in it with you, and I’ll challenge you when it counts, so you can break free from the old, unconscious patterns that keep running your life. With couples, I work to remove blame while preserving accountability, so each of you can see your part without the session turning into a trial.
aboutParagraph1: I grew up in a Los Angeles film and television family; my late father was a film and TV director. I was immersed in that world and its public life, and spent half my life working in film and the creative arts myself before becoming a therapist. I know it from the inside: the irregular work, the visibility, the way identity and output get tangled together. Many of my clients work in music, film, and the arts, and they don’t have to explain that world to me.
aboutParagraph2: I spent over a decade living as a renunciate Buddhist monk, immersed in contemplative yogic practice and daily meditation. That practice taught me to stay present with difficult experience without rushing to fix it, and it still shapes how I sit with every client.
aboutParagraph3: Today my work is anchored in Relational Gestalt and relational psychodynamic therapy, and integrates EMDR, the Gottman Method, relational mindfulness, and attachment-informed somatic emotional processing. I see adults and couples in person at my offices in Los Feliz, and by secure Zoom telehealth throughout California.
service1Description: Deep, exploratory work integrating EMDR, Relational Gestalt, relational psychodynamic therapy, and mindfulness-based Buddhist psychology for adults navigating burnout, anxiety, depression, trauma, and the fragmentation of modern identity.
service2Description: Restoring intimacy and communication through the Gottman Method, relational mindfulness, and attachment-informed somatic emotional processing, anchored in Relational Gestalt.
service3Description: Trauma-focused psychotherapy and EMDR for PTSD, attachment wounds, and experiences that still shape how you feel, relate, and respond.
service4Description: For artists, performers, and entertainment professionals: identity and worth, rejection, creative block, burnout, and finding your own voice.
ratesDescription1: Individual and couples sessions are 55 minutes, and 90-minute extended (double) sessions are available for deeper work.
ratesDescription2: Sessions booked directly through Depth Therapy are private pay. If your plan has out-of-network benefits, I provide monthly superbills you can submit for possible reimbursement.

oonSteps.title: Check your benefits.
oonSteps.text: Call your insurer and ask about out-of-network outpatient mental health benefits: your deductible, the reimbursement percentage, and whether pre-authorization is needed.

oonSteps.title: Pay for sessions directly.
oonSteps.text: Each month I send you a superbill, an itemized receipt with the codes insurers require.

oonSteps.title: Submit it.
oonSteps.text: Most insurers accept uploads through their app or website, and they reimburse you directly.

oonNote: If your plan is one I’m in network with, we’ll talk through the right way to bill during your consultation.
